analysis.summary: DR Congo (1 point, 3rd in Group K) face already-eliminated Uzbekistan in a must-win Matchday 3 decider. A DR Congo win takes them to 4 points and into serious contention as a best third-place qualifier; anything less eliminates them. Uzbekistan have the worst defensive record at the tournament (8 goals conceded in 2 games) and have no advancement incentive, creating a sharp motivation gap. DR Congo's squad quality — anchored by Premier League players Yoane Wissa, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Samuel Moutoussamy — comfortably exceeds Uzbekistan's in most positions.
analysis.home_form: DR Congo drew 1-1 with Portugal (Matchday 1, Houston) — Yoane Wissa equalised — and lost 1-0 to Colombia (Matchday 2, Guadalajara). Both performances showed defensive organisation: DR Congo conceded just 0.65 xG to Portugal and 0.98 xG to Colombia. Coach Sébastien Desabre used a back five in both matches but is expected to open up to a back four against Uzbekistan to generate more attacking impetus. Cédric Bakambu led the team's attacking threat with the most attempts in the tournament so far.
analysis.away_form: Uzbekistan, on their debut World Cup appearance, lost 3-1 to Colombia (Matchday 1) and 5-0 to Portugal (Matchday 2). Their goal difference stands at -7, the worst at the tournament. Abbosbek Fayzullaev scored Uzbekistan's historic first-ever World Cup goal (vs Colombia), while captain Eldor Shomurodov and Fayzullaev remain their main attacking outlets. Coach Fabio Cannavaro has been unable to address serial defensive lapses — Uzbekistan have conceded 8 goals in 180 minutes. The side are mathematically eliminated.
analysis.h2h: DR Congo and Uzbekistan have never previously met in international football. This is the first ever competitive encounter between the two nations.
injuries_news: DR Congo: No confirmed injuries or suspensions reported entering Matchday 3. Back five (5-3-2) expected to shift to 4-3-3 or 4-4-2 given the must-win context.
Uzbekistan: No confirmed injuries or suspensions. Midfielder Odiljon Hamrobekov carries a booking from Matchday 2 and will need to manage his discipline to avoid accumulation. Full squad available.
Referee: Felix Zwayer (Germany) appointed — an experienced FIFA referee. Specific card-rate data for this appointment unconfirmed from available sources.
key_factors: Qualification pressure asymmetry: DR Congo desperately need three points; Uzbekistan are already eliminated and have nothing to play for — this is a decisive motivational edge for the Leopards.
Uzbekistan's catastrophic defensive record (8 goals conceded in 2 games) is the worst at the tournament; DR Congo's forwards Wissa and Bakambu should find space.
DR Congo expected to abandon their back five and push forward with a more attacking shape, increasing both their offensive output and their exposure to Uzbekistan's counter-threat.
Coach Desabre's side has shown defensive discipline (conceded 2 in 2 games vs high-quality opposition), suggesting a clean sheet is realistic.
Group K co-matches (Colombia vs Portugal) happening simultaneously — DR Congo know exactly how many points they need; a win locks in 4 points and a strong third-place case.
Mercedes-Benz Stadium is a comfortable, air-conditioned indoor venue (Atlanta) — conditions neutral, no altitude or extreme heat factor.
Uzbekistan's best attacking threat is Fayzullaev, who will be tracked tightly by Moutoussamy and Pickel in central midfield.
